next.name: Silent Librarian
next.headline: Silent Librarian: phishing campaigns aimed at universities, per Malwarebytes
next.in_short: Malwarebytes reports that Silent Librarian ran spear phishing against universities from the 2020 academic year. The sites copied library and login pages. The vendor says it has seen only a small part of the operation.

sentences.t: Malwarebytes' Threat Intelligence Team reports that the actor known as Silent Librarian is also tracked as TA407 and COBALT DICKENS.
The report cites a March 2018 US Department of Justice indictment of nine Iranians for attacks on universities.
The actor has been actively targeting universities, according to Malwarebytes.
The report says that in August 2018 and 2019 the group again targeted the same kind of victims in over a dozen countries.
It says people at universities contribute to and access research that could be worth millions or billions of dollars.
According to Malwarebytes, the phishing sites imitate university library and single sign-on login pages.
The report says the actor uses Cloudflare for most of its phishing hostnames to hide the real hosting origin.
The new domain names follow the same pattern as previously reported, but swap the top level domain, the report says.

With outside help, the vendor identified some of the infrastructure on Iran-based hosts. The report says this may seem odd for an attacker and only possibly points to the group. It calls it simply another bulletproof hosting option.
The report attributes related subdomains to the same actor because registering them is known behaviour for the group. It says this is expected rather than confirmed.
Malwarebytes says the spear phishing campaigns have run since the 2020 academic year began.
The report says a customer tipped the vendor off in mid-September about a new active campaign.
It notes that in August 2018 and 2019 the group was also lining up for the new academic year.
The vendor says it has uncovered only a small portion of the phishing operation.
